questions.stem: In the reaction Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, what happens to the zinc?

options.text: It is reduced because it gains electrons
It is reduced because it loses oxygen
It is neither oxidised nor reduced
It is oxidised because it loses electrons

questions.explanation: Zinc is oxidised because it loses electrons: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻. In this redox reaction, zinc loses electrons (oxidation) while copper ions gain electrons (reduction). Zinc acts as the reducing agent.
